_note: The judgement layer. Everything in data/hazards.json that is NOT a copy of a
researched figure lives here, so the two can be argued with separately.
The researchers gave a rate, a set of severity tiers with death fractions, and
citations. They could not give: how much of a death toll is prompt rather than
famine (which decides whether a grain reserve helps), how much stratospheric
aerosol an event puts up and for how long, how much industry it destroys, how
world state should move the rate, or how hard one hazard leans on another.
Those are modelling calls and they are mine. Each carries a `why`.
PROMPT vs FAMINE is the call that matters most. Published global death figures
for aerosol events are famine numbers — Xia et al. 2022 separate ~27M direct
deaths from ~260M famine deaths at 5 Tg of soot, and ~360M from >5bn at 150 Tg.
Prompt deaths are not buffered by anything; famine deaths are what the food
system knobs act on. Getting this split wrong makes the whole food half of the

drop.grain-reserve-buffer-thinness: Not an event — a STATE, already carried by the reserveDays knob. Its worst tier is explicitly conditional on an abrupt sunlight reduction also happening, which the volcano, impact and nuclear hazards already roll for. Keeping it would double-count the same famine.
drop.grain-export-ban-cascade: Same defect: the severe tier is 'trade shutdown DURING a global production shock'. Carried by the tradeOpenness knob and by the asymmetric trade term in resilience().
drop.jit-logistics-and-settlement-spof: Its own severity tiers are conditional on another shock; the researcher labelled its key parameters 'MULTIPLIER USE' in the source packet. Folded into the infrastructure hazard and the reserve knob.
drop.resilient-food-deployment-failure: Explicitly defined as 'a shock beginning in a year in which resilient-food capacity remains undeployed' — i.e. it is a conditional severity modifier wearing an event's clothes. It IS the resilientFoodShare knob.
